content.text: I'm starting the campaign. The phase list was too long to display, so I got a valid model receipt a different way: a MEGNet band gap for V2O5. Next I'll measure the composition closest to BiVO4.

input.verdict: Weakly uninformative-to-supportive. The MEGNet HSE gap for V2O5 is 2.83 eV, which is near or above the 2.72 eV photon energy, so V-only phases absorb poorly at 455 nm. The most promising absorber is BiVO4 (about 2.4-2.5 eV) with a small amount of Cu. Index 60 (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.17, V 0.43) is the candidate closest to Bi:V = 1:1 with the least Cu, so it is measured first.

input.verdict: Supportive. The MEGNet HSE gap for Bi2O3 is 2.34 eV, below the 2.72 eV photon energy. So the Bi-rich corner (Bi2O3/BiVO4 with some CuBi2O4, all with visible-light gaps) should absorb at 455 nm. Measuring index 124 (Bi 0.63) explores the second, V-poor half of the library.

toolu_018qynQEUJeKJfxPL34tihoj.verdict: Supportive. The MEGNet HSE gap for Bi2O3 is 2.34 eV, below the 2.72 eV photon energy. So the Bi-rich corner (Bi2O3/BiVO4 with some CuBi2O4, all with visible-light gaps) should absorb at 455 nm. Measuring index 124 (Bi 0.63) explores the second, V-poor half of the library.

input.verdict: Against Cu-rich compositions. The MEGNet HSE gap for CuO is 0.32 eV, so Cu-rich phases are narrow-gap, recombination-prone and not photoanodic; index 124 gave zero photocurrent. So the best choice is to stay in the BiVO4-like, low-Cu region where index 60 gave 12.6 uA. Index 22 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46) sits next to 60 with slight V excess, which usually favors monoclinic BiVO4.

The MEGNet HSE gap for CuO is 0.32 eV, so Cu-rich phases are narrow-gap, recombination-prone and not photoanodic; index 124 gave zero photocurrent. So the best choice is to stay in the BiVO4-like, low-Cu region where index 60 gave 12.6 uA. Index 22 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46) sits next to 60 with slight V excess, which usually favors monoclinic BiVO4.

input.rationale: Index 22 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46) had the highest measured photocurrent, 26.5 uA. That is about twice index 60 (12.6 uA, Bi 0.40, Cu 0.17, V 0.43). The Bi-rich, V-poor index 124 gave zero. The results point to a BiVO4-like, low-Cu phase with a slight V excess as the active photoanode. MEGNet gaps agree: Bi2O3 at 2.34 eV absorbs visible light, V2O5 at 2.83 eV sits at the edge of the 2.72 eV photon energy, and CuO at 0.32 eV is narrow-gap and unsuitable.

rejected.reason: Measured zero photocurrent. The Bi-rich, Cu-containing, V-poor region (like the p-type CuBi2O4) is not photoanodic.
Measured 12.6 uA, below index 22. Being closer to Bi:V = 1 with less V excess did not help.
The CuO MEGNet gap is 0.32 eV and Cu-rich phases are p-type or narrow-gap, so they are unlikely to work as photoanodes. No budget was spent there.

content.text:
I submitted index 22 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 26.5 µA. The whole merit budget of three measurements is used, so most of the library is still unmeasured and a better composition may exist.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 60 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | 12.6 µA |
| 124 | 0.63 / 0.23 / 0.14 | 0 |
| 22 | 0.36 / 0.18 / 0.46 | 26.5 µA |

- **Why these three:** I measured 60 first because it is the most BiVO4-like candidate (a known photoanode material) with the least copper. Index 124 checked the bismuth-rich, low-vanadium half of the library, which gave nothing. I spent the last measurement on 22, next to 60 but with slightly more vanadium, and it doubled the result.
- **Model checks:** The phase list was too large to display and I had no way to read the saved file, so I didn't have the library's phase IDs. After three guessed IDs failed, I used band-gap predictions for simple oxides I could name instead: V2O5 2.83 eV, Bi2O3 2.34 eV, CuO 0.32 eV, against 2.72 eV light. They're only a rough guide to which regions absorb the light and suit a photoanode; they don't describe the actual mixed phases.
- **Not done:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phase present at index 22 is not confirmed. The optimum may lie at somewhat higher vanadium near 22, which the tool that suggests the next measurement also favoured (index 26); I didn't measure it.
